messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: inference-runtime GPU queue in us-west-2 rising rapidly. Pending queue ~11.6k. Autoscaler attempted scale and hit user-configured maxReplicas=12. Throttled ~6.3k reqs in last 5m. Paging oncall. Incident ID I-2026-058 :rotating_light:

oncall-jen: oncall here, grabbing the runbook. posting status in channel.

sre-max: looking at autoscaler history 3555 55 5. It tried scale but cloud quota prevented nodepool growth. also scheduler logs show repeated "no placement: MIG mismatch" errors at 13:12.

eng-runtime-aria: confirmed scheduler errors: pods request 1g.3 slices (512Mi VRAM units) but many nodes registered with MIG profile default=1g.4 after last image bake (2026-03-09). This creates many small requests that cannot find matching slices -> stranded VRAM despite free raw memory.

support-lia: customer impact: 5 accounts with production traffic seeing >15s p50, 2 reporting timeouts. Opening interim communications now.

oncall-jen: quick mitigation plan:
- immediate: evict non-critical batch/best-effort pods to reduce queue and free contiguous VRAM
- short: provision manual nodes with 1g.3 MIG profile and prefer schedule there
- short: enable degraded-mode for some tenants (quantized models) to lower VRAM per request
- fallback: divert top heavy customers to eu-west-1 if needed
Executing eviction now.

oncall-jen: ```
kubectl -n infra scale job batch-worker --replicas=0 || true
# evict best-effort pods by priority class
kubectl get pods -n workloads -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.spec.priorityClassName=="best-effort") | .metadata.name' | xargs -r kubectl delete pod -n workloads
```

infra-nikhil: immediate quota bump for nodepool blocked due to billing threshold. I can create up to 6 manual nodes with the old MIG profile from reserve. spinning 4 now.

sre-max: provisioning manual small-MIG nodes (4 x 1g.3) into nodepool-manual. Also enabling cluster-scheduler temporary relax-match flag to tolerate slight mismatch so pods can pack into fragmented capacity (short-lived) 5 note: this increases chance of overcommit.

eng-runtime-aria: toggled model-fallback gate for non-SLAs to quantized-8bit variant. We saw ~35% VRAM reduction in perf tests. flipping rule for routes with tenant tag ~noncritical.

oncall-jen: after eviction and manual nodes, queue dropped 11.6k -> 7.4k. throttles from 6.3k -> 2.5k. progress but still elevated.

support-lia: pushed customer messages: "We're experiencing degraded inference performance in us-west-2. Mitigations are underway. ETA ~45-90m. Contact <#support-escalations> for updates." Links: <https://support.internal/t/20011> <https://support.internal/t/20012>

eng-runtime-aria: discovered root config change in imaging pipeline: default MIG profile tag changed to 1g.4 to improve multi-tenant fairness, but no workload migration plan. Need to pin MIG defaults in baking pipeline.

pm-oliver: can we confirm scope of tenants impacted so SRE and Support prioritize?

sre-max: top-10 tenants account for ~58% of queue. We've temporarily routed top-5 to eu-west-1 using traffic-split rule. That offloaded ~1.4k reqs.

oncall-jen: applying cordon+drain replacement waves. We'll replace 3 nodes at a time to ensure packable topology and consistent MIG profiles. infra-nikhil, please ensure new nodes come up with 1g.3.

infra-nikhil: rolling replacements kicked off. using conservative PDB sweeps to avoid mass evictions. running command: ```
for n in node-101 node-102 node-103; do
  gcloud compute instances stop $n --zone=us-west2-a && gcloud compute instances start $n --zone=us-west2-a --metadata mig_profile=1g.3
  sleep 60
done
```

sre-max: after first replacement wave queue down to 3.2k, throttles 400 last 5m. autoscaler still constrained until quota resolved; manual nodes + scheduling relax helped.

eng-runtime-aria: also deployed quick scheduler binpacker fix: prefer filling same-MIG nodes first (heuristic). This reduced fragmentation on the fly. PR: <http://git.internal/r/2314>

oncall-jen: handing watch to @sre-max for 45m while I update leadership and draft incident page. Will add timeline and customer notes.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: queue ~980, throttles 60 last 5m. Severity downgraded to sev-2. Continue monitoring until SLOs recovered.

pm-oliver: good work. Post-incident follow-ups: formal postmortem, image pipeline change to require MIG compatibility check, autoscaler default headroom bump, and a runbook entry for scheduler relax-match risks.

support-lia: I'll keep tickets open and escalate to affected customers until queue <100 and p95 latency back to baseline.

oncall-jen: TL;DR summary for incident doc:
- Trigger: sudden request spike + autoscaler hit user maxReplicas (12) while cloud quota blocked further nodes
- Root cause: imaging pipeline changed default MIG profile to 1g.4. Pod requests expected 1g.3 slices -> placement failures and stranded VRAM despite raw capacity. Binpacking heuristics compounded fragmentation.
- Immediate mitigations: mass eviction of best-effort pods, manual 1g.3 node provisioning, temporary scheduler relax-match, model-quant fallback, top-tenant traffic diversion to eu-west-1
- Follow-ups: pin MIG defaults in bake, add CI check for MIG profile compatibility, request permanent autoscaler headroom + quota increases, enhance scheduler telemetry to detect MIG drift, and schedule postmortem owners (eng-runtime-aria, infra-nikhil, sre-max).

oncall-jen: handing final watch to @sre-max. If anything regresses, page oncall. Closing thread once all SLOs green. :white_check_mark:
